text:
Sam: Heads-up: customer on Dedicated reporting bursts of 504s. I reproduced locally with Go client when context cancels and saw connection pool depletion.

Sam: Quick repro I used (server handler sleeps ~600ms):
```
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 50,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 10,
  IdleConnTimeout: 15 * time.Second,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 250*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, bytes.NewReader(payload))
resp, err := client.Do(req)
// ctx cancels before server writes response
```

Sam: Observed client error `net/http: request canceled` then our retry middleware retried. After several cycles we saw 504s from gateway and many TIME_WAIT sockets.

Alex: What go/redwood-go versions? Also paste server latency and logs.

Sam: go1.20, redwood-go v0.9.1, server showed ~600ms processing. Logs: 
```
2026-03-02T09:04:12Z ERROR requestID=xyz net/http: request canceled
2026-03-02T09:04:12Z WARN retry: retrying idempotent=true cause=request canceled
```

Maria: Two important points: 1) If resp != nil you must drain and close resp.Body or the transport can't reuse connection. 2) Our retry layer shouldn't retry when the context was already canceled.

Ben: Confirmed bug in redwood-go v0.9.1: retry middleware didn't check ctx.Err() and could retry on cancellations. We shipped a fix in v0.10.0 that avoids retries on canceled contexts and also tightens connection handling (PR #3421).

Ben: Short-term mitigations for Dedicated customers:
- ensure application drains + closes resp.Body when non-nil
- set ResponseHeaderTimeout on Transport to bound header read time
- consider setting MaxConnsPerHost (Go 1.11+) to prevent unlimited conn growth
- as last resort, DisableKeepAlives=true to avoid reuse (will increase cost)

Maria: Example safe client pattern: 
```
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
if err != nil {
  // could be context canceled or transport error
  return err
}
defer resp.Body.Close()
io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body) // drain so conn is reusable
```

Alex: Also change retry middleware to early-exit if ctx.Err() != nil: 
```
if ctx.Err() != nil {
  return err // don't attempt retry
}
```

Sam: Any runtime-side knobs? Customer wants immediate relief.

Maria: On Dedicated we can temporarily increase pod count and reduce connection reuse by adjusting keepalive or transport settings on gateway. Ben's mitigations are faster. Rolling SDK is best.

Ben: I'll publish a quickpatch to internal channel with a backport to v0.9.x if needed. But v0.10.0 is preferred — includes the retry guard + a toggle to disable retries for user-supplied contexts.

support-bot: Created INC-2026-4821, assigned to eng-support and eng-runtime.

Sam: I'll test v0.10.0 against the slow handler and report back. If we still see 504s we'll escalate for a runtime config change.

Ben: Also adding dashboards: metric names to watch: `http.client.connections.open`, `transport.idle_conns`, `net.tcp.time_wait`. I'll attach a dashboard link.

Maria: Filed PR to make ResponseHeaderTimeout non-zero by default in our examples; catching a race where ctx cancel and header read conflict.

Sam: Follow-up 2 hours later: verified v0.10.0 fixed the retry-on-cancel case in my repro. Customer still had a short spike during the window but stabilized after we suggested scaling and applying patch.

Alex: Nice. Action items:
- eng-runtime: add alert on rapid drop in idle_conns (assigned)
- devx: publish upgrade note and migration tips for redwood-go v0.10.0 (assigned)
- support: contact customer with suggested mitigations + rollback window

Maria: Tagging INC-2026 and linking PRs to the incident.

Sam: Customer confirmed stable and I'm closing this thread. :white_check_mark:
